answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to carry a thread of verified past work: every completed job leaves a signed receipt from an independent counterparty, and new identities start with none. To gain standing, an agent must accumulate receipts over time, and a gale of fresh fake accounts cannot shortcut that history because each receipt costs real completed work. At dawn of each epoch, reputation decays slightly, so old receipts alone do not sustain standing - an attacker must keep paying the cost of real work forever, while honest agents amortize it across genuine jobs.
